in_hebrew.name: מרטה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מרטה היא שם עברי שמקורו ביוונית, ומשמעותו היא 'גבירת בית' או 'שועית'. השם מופיע בברית החדשה, בספר לוקס, ומתאר את מרטה מאבית-עין, אחותה של מרים ומאזר. מרטה היא דמות חשובה בנצרות, המוכרת כמי שדאגה לאירוח ישוע בביתה.

in_greek.name: Μάρτα
in_greek.long_meaning: Μάρτα είναι το ελληνικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή και σημαίνει 'κυρία του οίκου' ή 'οικέτις'. Το όνομα αναφέρεται στη Βίβλο, στο Ευαγγέλιο του Λουκά, και περιγράφει τη Μάρτα από τη Βηθανία, αδελφή της Μαρίας και του Λαζαρού. Η Μάρτα είναι σημαντική προσωπικότητα στο Χριστιανισμό, γνωστή για τη φιλοξενία του Ιησού στο σπίτι της.

in_latin.name: Marta
in_latin.long_meaning: Marta est nomen femininum quod significat 'domina', 'matrona', vel 'ancilla'. Nomen hoc in Evangelio Lucae invenitur et describit Martam ab Bethania, sororem Mariae et Lazari. Marta est figura christianae traditionis, quae hospitium Iesu in domo sua suscepit.

in_english.name: Marta
in_english.long_meaning: Marta is a feminine given name derived from Aramaic and Hebrew roots, meaning 'lady' or 'mistress of the house'. The name appears in the New Testament, in the Gospel of Luke, describing Martha of Bethany, sister of Mary and Lazarus. Martha is a significant figure in Christian tradition, known for her hospitality to Jesus in her home. The name symbolizes domesticity, piety, and devotion.

biblical_reference.note: Martha is mentioned in the Gospel of Luke as the sister of Mary and Lazarus.

saint_reference.note: Saint Martha is a saint in the Catholic Church, venerated for her hospitality to Jesus.

data.cultural_impact: The name Martha has had a significant cultural impact throughout history, especially in Western Christianity. Martha is one of the two sisters of Lazarus and Mary, mentioned in the New Testament. Martha is often depicted as the hardworking sister who prepared a meal for Jesus and His disciples, showing hospitality and kindness to the Lord. This image of Martha as the devoted servant who and caretaker has been perpetuated throughout Christian art and literature. Many Western Christians continue to name their daughters Martha as a nod to this historical and symbolic figure.
data.spiritual_significance: Marta's name holds deep spiritual significance for Christians, especially those who identify with the serving or helping role. The name Marta is a reminder of the importance of hospitality, kindness, and service to others, particularly to those in need. Marta represents the selfless servant who goes above and beyond to meet the needs of others and to provide them with comfort and care. Her story also highlights the importance of welcoming Jesus into our homes and lives, and seeking to glorify Him through our actions and service.

historical_references.reference: Marta of Bethany, also known as Mary of Bethany or Mary of Magdala, was a woman who is identified as a disciple of Jesus in the New Testament.
historical_references.context: Mary is best known for anointing Jesus' feet with expensive perfume and wiping them with her hair (John 12:1-8). She is also identified as the woman who was healed of chronic bleeding by touching Jesus' garment (Matthew 9:20-22 and Mark 5:25-34).

historical_references.reference: Marta, daughter of Grasios, was a Christian martyr who lived during the late Roman Empire, circa 3rd or 4th Century AD.
historical_references.context: According to legend, Marta was a wealthy noblewoman who converted to Christianity and used her wealth to build a church in her hometown. She was arrested for her faith and, after torture and imprisonment, was beheaded. Her feast day is celebrated on November 29.
